details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library with covert account-manipulation code injected into its socket layer. When a WhatsApp session connects, the library silently forces the linked account to follow a third-party channel and then mutes it, so the user neither sees nor notices the subscription. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js the channel JID 120363422352987107@newsletter is hardcoded and an autoJoinChannels() routine issues the follow and mute queries 15 seconds after connection.update reports "open". lib/Socket/messages-recv.js contains a second, deliberately hidden copy of the same operation: decimal char-code arrays are reassembled at runtime with String.fromCharCode into the channel JID and into the method names newsletterFollow and newsletterMute, then invoked 30 seconds after connect with 3- and 10-second sleeps between calls. The package README states that newsletterFollow() is only called explicitly by the application and that no automatic join happens when a socket is created, contradicting the shipped code. The same file also auto-reacts to messages arriving from that channel with a randomly picked emoji, acting as the user. No credential, token, environment or file exfiltration was found; the only external destination is WhatsApp's own service (the channel JID 120363422352987107@newsletter).
